ConsoleBuffer

ConsoleBuffer holds the characters and colors used to draw a control. A custom UIElement receives its buffer in RenderContent and writes into it using local coordinates.

Drawing Text and Cells

ContentRect excludes the control's border. Drawing methods are bounded by the buffer, but you should also clip content to ContentRect if it must not overwrite the border. The Badge example shows text-element clipping.

Drawing Methods

  • SetPixel: Sets the character, foreground and background of a cell.
  • WriteString / WriteStringWrapped: Writes a string directly or wraps it to a width.
  • FillRect / DrawRect: Fills an area or draws a box.
  • WriteBuffer: Combines a child buffer at a local position. respectBackground defaults to true.
  • CreateSubBuffer: Creates a buffer from a bounded subregion.
  • GetStringWidth / GetTextElementWidth: Measures best-effort terminal cell widths.
  • Screenshot: Returns text output, with optional color escape sequences.

The buffer indexer uses [row, column], while drawing methods use (x, y). ConsoleWindowManager handles presenting the frame; a custom control should not call RenderToConsole itself.

Capturing a Render

The output examples in these docs use a 64 by 12 window capture, without ANSI colors. Trailing whitespace is removed. FilePicker's directory caption is replaced with /demo so it does not show a machine-specific path.

Display widths and shaping for combining characters and emoji can still depend on the terminal and font.
